assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Fossil fuels
items.clue: Coal, crude oil and natural gas.

items.label: Incomplete combustion
items.clue: Burning in a limited supply of oxygen, forming carbon monoxide or soot.

items.label: Greenhouse effect
items.clue: Gases in the atmosphere absorb and re-emit infrared, warming the surface.

items.label: Photosynthesis
items.clue: Light energy is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.

questions.stem: Ethanol, C₂H₅OH, undergoes complete combustion in oxygen. What amount of oxygen, O₂, reacts with 1.00 mol of ethanol?
questions.explanation: C₂H₅OH(l) + 3O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g) + 3H₂O(l). The products contain 2 × 2 + 3 × 1 = 7 O atoms; ethanol supplies 1 of them, so O₂ supplies 6 O atoms, which is 3 O₂. So 1.00 mol of ethanol reacts with 3.00 mol of O₂.

questions.stem: Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of ethanol?
questions.explanation: In a very limited supply of oxygen the carbon of ethanol is deposited as carbon (soot), while the hydrogen still forms water. The equation is balanced: the products contain 3 O atoms, 1 from ethanol and 2 from O₂.

questions.stem: Coal has a greater tendency than natural gas to undergo incomplete combustion. Which statement gives a reason for this?

options.text: Coal contains impurities, and these, not its carbon, form the soot and carbon monoxide.
Coal needs more oxygen per gram than methane, as only the carbon in a fuel uses up oxygen.
Methane is a clean fuel, so its carbon cannot form carbon monoxide or soot.
Coal is a solid, so oxygen reaches only its surface, whereas gas mixes fully with air.

questions.explanation: A gaseous fuel such as methane can mix thoroughly with air before it burns, so every molecule has oxygen nearby. Solid coal, which is mostly carbon, reacts only where oxygen reaches its surface, so the oxygen supply to the carbon is easily limited and CO and soot form.

questions.stem: Which equation correctly represents the combustion of an element in excess oxygen?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus is a non-metal that burns in excess oxygen to form phosphorus(V) oxide, P₄O₁₀. Every formula is correct (oxygen as O₂) and the equation is balanced: 4 P and 10 O atoms on each side.

questions.stem: Methane burns in a limited supply of oxygen. Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: In a very limited supply of oxygen the carbon of methane is deposited as carbon (soot), while the hydrogen still forms water; 1 C, 4 H and 2 O atoms on each side.

questions.stem: Octane, C₈H₁₈, is a component of petrol, which is refined from crude oil. Use the following data: 5470 kJ of energy is released when 1 mol of octane burns completely; A_r: H 1.01, C 12.01, O 16.00. What mass of CO₂ is added to the atmosphere for every 1.00 × 10³ kJ of energy released by burning octane?
questions.explanation: 2C₈H₁₈ + 25O₂ → 16CO₂ + 18H₂O, so 1 mol of octane gives 8 mol of CO₂ (8 × 44.01 = 352.1 g) and releases 5470 kJ. Per 1.00 × 10³ kJ: 352.1 × 1000/5470 = 64.4 g of CO₂.

questions.stem: When the equation for the complete combustion of octane, C₈H₁₈, is balanced with a coefficient of 2 for octane, what is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: 2C₈H₁₈ forms 16CO₂ and 18H₂O, which contain 16 × 2 + 18 = 50 O atoms. Each O₂ supplies two O atoms, so 25 O₂ are needed: 2C₈H₁₈(l) + 25O₂(g) → 16CO₂(g) + 18H₂O(l).

questions.stem: Use the following data for the energy released when 1 mol of each fuel burns completely: coal (modelled as pure carbon, C) 394 kJ; natural gas (methane, CH₄) 891 kJ; petrol (modelled as octane, C₈H₁₈) 5470 kJ. A_r: H 1.01, C 12.01, O 16.00. Which conclusion is supported by these data?

options.text: Octane releases the most energy per gram of the three fuels.
Octane adds the least CO₂ per kJ of energy released of the three.
Methane releases the most energy per gram of the three fuels.
Methane adds no CO₂ to the atmosphere when it is burned as a fuel.

questions.explanation: Energy per gram = energy per mole ÷ molar mass: carbon 394/12.01 = 32.8 kJ g⁻¹; methane 891/16.05 = 55.5 kJ g⁻¹; octane 5470/114.26 = 47.9 kJ g⁻¹. Methane releases the most energy per gram.

questions.stem: Burning fossil fuels increases the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. How does this increase lead to warming of the Earth's surface?

options.text: CO₂ absorbs visible and ultraviolet light coming from the Sun, heating the air.
CO₂ absorbs infrared radiation emitted by the surface and re-emits some of it back.
CO₂ destroys the ozone layer, so more of the Sun's radiation reaches the surface.
CO₂ forms a layer high in the atmosphere that reflects the surface's heat back down.

questions.explanation: Sunlight passes through the atmosphere and warms the surface, which emits infrared radiation. CO₂ molecules absorb this infrared and re-emit it in all directions, some back towards the surface, so more CO₂ means a warmer surface (the enhanced greenhouse effect).

questions.stem: Use the following data for the energy released when 1 mol of each fuel burns completely: coal (modelled as pure carbon, C) 394 kJ; petrol (modelled as octane, C₈H₁₈) 5470 kJ. A_r: H 1.01, C 12.01, O 16.00. How many times greater is the mass of CO₂ added to the atmosphere per kJ of energy released when coal burns than when octane burns?
